questions.question:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

a) is credited with saying

b) do not dry your feet

c) If you want to leave your footprint on the sands of time,

d) Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, former President of India
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'DACB'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given question is an example of a **Para Jumble.**
 
• We know that the first statement of a para jumbled question is usually **an independent general statement, a noun, a universal fact, etc**.
 
• **Sentence D** will be the first sentence because it is an introductory sentence and independent of all the other sentences.
 
• **Sentence A** will be the next sentence because '**credited with saying'** is directly connected with the first sentence.
 
• **Sentence C** will be the next sentence because it tells the '**action'** connect with the previous one.
 
• Lastly, **Sentence B** will be used.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, former President of India is credited with saying If you want to leave your footprint on the sands of time, do not dry your feet.*

questions.question: If cot 75° = 2 - √3 Find the value of cot 15°
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

We know the complementary angle property: tan θ = cot(90° − θ).

⇒ tan 15° = cot(90° − 15°) = cot 75° = 2 − √3

We also know that cot θ = 1 ÷ tan θ.

⇒ cot 15° = 1 ÷ (2 − √3)

Rationalizing the denominator by multiplying with its conjugate (2 + √3):

⇒ cot 15° = (2 + √3) ÷ (2² − (√3)²) = (2 + √3) ÷ (4 − 3) = 2 + √3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 + √3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

cot 75° = 2 − √3

**Formula Used:**

cot(A − B) = (cot A × cot B + 1) ÷ (cot B − cot A)

**Calculation:**

We can write 15° as (45° − 30°).

⇒ cot 15° = cot(45° − 30°)

⇒ cot 15° = (cot 45° × cot 30° + 1) ÷ (cot 30° − cot 45°)

Substitute the standard trigonometric values (cot 45° = 1 and cot 30° = √3):

⇒ cot 15° = (1 × √3 + 1) ÷ (√3 − 1)

⇒ cot 15° = (√3 + 1) ÷ (√3 − 1)

To rationalize, multiply both the numerator and the denominator by (√3 + 1):

⇒ cot 15° = [(√3 + 1) × (√3 + 1)] ÷ [(√3 − 1) × (√3 + 1)]

⇒ cot 15° = (3 + 1 + 2√3) ÷ (3 − 1)

⇒ cot 15° = (4 + 2√3) ÷ 2

⇒ cot 15° = 2 × (2 + √3) ÷ 2

⇒ cot 15° = 2 + √3

**∴ The correct answer is 2 + √3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Ratios of Complementary Angles

Two angles are complementary if their sum is exactly 90°. Key relations include: sin(90° − θ) = cos θ, tan(90° − θ) = cot θ, and sec(90° − θ) = cosec θ.

Important Values for 15° and 75°

sin 15° = cos 75° = (√6 − √2) ÷ 4 
 cos 15° = sin 75° = (√6 + √2) ÷ 4 
 tan 15° = cot 75° = 2 − √3 
 cot 15° = tan 75° = 2 + √3

Rationalization Rule

When a denominator contains a surd of the form (a − √b), it can be eliminated by multiplying both the numerator and the denominator by its conjugate pair (a + √b) based on the algebraic identity (x − y)(x + y) = x² − y².
</p

questions.question: A thief was spotted by a policeman from a distance of 225 metres. When the policeman started the chase, the thief also started running. If the speed of the thief was 11 km/h and that of the policeman was 13 km/h, how far would the thief have run, before the policeman caught up with him ?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the time taken by both moving objects is constant, the ratio of the distance covered is equal to the ratio of their speeds.

Speed ratio (Thief : Policeman) = 11 : 13

Distance ratio (Thief : Policeman) = 11 : 13

Difference in distance covered = 13 parts − 11 parts = 2 parts

Given the initial distance difference is 225 m ⇒ 2 parts = 225 m ⇒ 1 part = 112.5 m

Distance run by the thief = 11 parts = 11 × 112.5 = 1237.5 metres

**∴ The correct answer is 1237.5 metres.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial distance between policeman and thief = 225 m

Speed of thief = 11 km/h

Speed of policeman = 13 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66be807f0a7af36f7022e9bb9487558704e54a09eed7b85ee25b428d01b045a1.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Relative speed (same direction) = Speed₁ − Speed₂

Time = Distance ÷ Relative Speed

Distance = Speed × Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Relative speed = 13 − 11 = 2 km/h

⇒ Relative speed in m/s = 2 × (5/18) = 5/9 m/s

⇒ Time taken to catch the thief = Distance ÷ Relative speed = 225 ÷ (5/9)

⇒ Time taken = 225 × (9/5) = 45 × 9 = 405 seconds

⇒ Speed of thief in m/s = 11 × (5/18) = 55/18 m/s

⇒ Distance covered by thief before getting caught = Speed of thief × Time taken

⇒ Distance = (55/18) × 405 = 55 × 22.5

⇒ Distance = 1237.5 m

**∴ The correct answer is 1237.5 metres.**

Relative Speed (Same Direction)

When two bodies are moving in the same direction, their relative speed is the difference between their individual speeds: S = S₁ − S₂.

Relative Speed (Opposite Direction)

When two bodies are moving in opposite directions towards each other, their relative speed is the sum of their individual speeds: S = S₁ + S₂.

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from km/h to m/s, multiply the value by 5/18. To convert speed from m/s to km/h, multiply the value by 18/5.

questions.question: Which of the following is divisible by 3 ?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Check the sum of digits for each number; if the sum is divisible by 3, the number is also divisible by 3.

Sum of digits of 7345932 = 7+3+4+5+9+3+2 = 33.

33 is divisible by 3 (33 ÷ 3 = 11).

**∴ The correct option is A.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: Numbers in options A, B, C, and D.

Formula: Divisibility rule of 3 states that a number is divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is a multiple of 3.

⇒ Option A: 7345932 → Sum = 7+3+4+5+9+3+2 = 33

⇒ 33 ÷ 3 = 11 (Divisible by 3)

⇒ Option B: 5439763 → Sum = 5+4+3+9+7+6+3 = 37 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ Option C: 3642589 → Sum = 3+6+4+2+5+8+9 = 37 (Not divisible by 3)

⇒ Option D: 3262735 → Sum = 3+2+6+2+7+3+5 = 28 (Not divisible by 3)

**∴ The correct option is A.**

**__Additional Information__**

Divisibility by 9

A number is divisible by 9 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 9.

Divisibility by 6

A number is divisible by 6 if it is divisible by both 2 (the number is even) and 3.

Divisibility by 4

A number is divisible by 4 if its last two digits are divisible by 4.

Divisibility by 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd positions and even positions is 0 or a multiple of 11.</p

• **Joseph Louis Proust **was a French chemist. He was best known for his discovery of the law of definite proportions in **1794**, stating that chemical compounds always combine in constant proportions.

• In Chemistry, **stoichiometry** is based on this law.
 
 
• **Statement:**__ Chemical compounds consist of elements that are always present at fixed ratios (in terms of their mass) according to the law of definite proportions as well as the law of constant proportions. In this ratio, neither the source nor the method of preparation of the chemical compound is relevant.
 
• __**Explanation:**__ Chemical compounds, according to the law of constant proportions, are made of elements present in a fixed ratio by mass. The concentration of each element in a compound will always be the same by mass regardless of the source of the sample.
 
 
 
• **Nitrogen **and **oxygen **atoms are always in a** 1:2 **ratio in the nitrogen dioxide molecule (NO2).

questions.question: Find the correct chemical formula of nitromethane.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__CH₃NO₂__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Nitromethane (CH3NO2) is an important organic chemical raw material with a wide variety of applications as well as one of the most common pollutants.
 
• It is a polar liquid commonly used as a solvent in a variety of industrial applications such as in extractions, as a reaction medium, and as a cleaning solvent.
 
• Nitromethane is produced industrially by combining propane and nitric in the gas phase at **350–450 °C** (662–842 °F). 
 
• It is slow to deprotonate. 
 
• Nitromethane is a** colorless, oily liquid with a mild disagreeable or fruity odor.** It is used as a propellant, fuel additive, rocket fuel, and solvent, and in making dyes, textiles, pharmaceuticals, and explosives.
 
• Nitromethane-or **CH3NO2**-is one member of a family of explosive compounds that contain nitrogen and oxygen.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ch₃NO** is the formula used to refer to Nitrosomethane.
 
• **Urea is a nitrogenous compound formed in the liver.** It has a chemical formula of **CH****₄N₂****O.** It is also known as **Carbamide or Ureophil.**
 
• **CH₃NO₃** is the chemical formula of **Methyl Nitrate.**

questions.question: Which of the following is a type of bryophyte that lives in many environments and is characterised by its small, flattened leaves, root-like rhizoids, and peristome?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Funaria__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Funaria is **a genus of approximately 210 species of moss**.
 
• **Funaria hygrometrica** is the most common species.
 
• Funaria hygrometrica is called “**cord moss**” because of the twisted seta which is very hygroscopic and untwists when moist.
 
• The name is derived from the Latin word **“funis”, meaning "a rope"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/94cf770556991a7323868ee33045fd4ec3d608b0e2dba0bd28f126d7c9014c18.png] ​

• Seta: the stalk of a moss sporangium, or occasionally in a liverwort
 
• Rhizoid: a rootlike structure that acts as support and anchors the plant to its substrate
 
• Peristome: one or two rings of tooth-like appendages surrounding the opening of the capsule of many mosses that aid in spreading spores
